overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session on May 18, 2011 for litigation and confidential-document purposes, but faulted the vague notice and the minutes' missing document list.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board cited 'legal matters' as the sole reason for its May 18, 2011 executive session, which is not an enumerated Open Meeting Law purpose.
allegations.key_passage: The Board discussed strategies with respect to imminently threatened or pending litigation after reviewing a communication from counsel. This was appropriate under Purpose 3.

allegations.summary: The posted notice listed the executive session topic only as a 'Legal Matter' under G.L. c. 30A, §21(a), which the complainant said was not a valid purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Board had appropriate reasons to enter executive session, the Board failed to provide sufficient notice to the public about its reasons for entering executive session.

allegations.summary: The executive session minutes did not include a list of the documents and exhibits the Board used, as G.L. c. 30A, §22(a) requires.
allegations.key_passage: The executive session minutes we reviewed did not include a list of any documents or exhibits used by the Board

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law.
Attach a list of documents and other exhibits used at the May 18, 2011 meeting to the final, approved executive session minutes once they are released to the public.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the requirements of the Open Meeting Law, and further order the Board to attach "a list of documents and other exhibits used" at the Board's May 18, 2011 meeting to the final, approved executive session minutes once they are released to the public.
